text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime-p99-regression detector triggered for service `/v1/stream` (p99 > 800ms) — SLO breach. AlertID: reg-20240315-001. Paging oncall.

maria: saw the alert. digging into dashboards now (console -> realtime/p95-p99). p99 jumped at ~1718507720 and stayed elevated.

jordan: i'm on pager, taking lead. travis is OOO, cc @sam for infra help.

sam: thanks @jordan. first quick checks: any recent deploys to streaming cluster? k8s events? autoscaler spikes?

maria: no deploys in last 2 hours. metrics look like a sharp tail-latency increase for streaming sessions with long contexts. prefix cache miss rate up ~40%.

leo: copying graphs: p95 stayed ~120ms, p99 moved from 420ms -> 920ms. throughput stable. suggests tail events, maybe KV cache pressure or worker GC.

maria: running `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=streamer -o wide` now.

sam: also check kvcache eviction: `redis-cluster: role=primary` latency?

maria: pasted logs snippet: ```
[2024-03-15T12:02:01Z] stream-handler-7: WARN slow_token_fetch  user=svc-123 latency=202ms
[2024-03-15T12:02:02Z] stream-handler-3: ERROR stall_detected seq=1873 stall_ms=1500
[2024-03-15T12:02:04Z] stream-handler-7: INFO request_completed latency=950ms status=200 model=gpt-open-6b
```

jordan: interesting — stall_detected lines. Could be long KV cache miss path + model kernel switch. Any correlation with quantized model rollout?

maria: we rolled a quantized variant to a canary subset yesterday (model: gpt-open-6b-quant-canary) but traffic routing should be <5%. No spike seen in canary logs.

ops-runbook-bot: Suggested playbook: throttle large streaming sessions, enable fallback-to-smaller-model route, restart affected pods if mem/GC anomalies.

sam: quick mitigations we can do now: 1) enable per-session token cap to reduce very long contexts 2) flip routing for heavy sessions to model `gpt-open-3b` (fast-fallback) 3) temporarily disable canary if suspected. Thoughts?

jordan: do 1 and 2 now. I'll coordinate with routing-config. Maria, can you apply a temp route rule to catch sessions with >3000 tokens?

maria: applying rule: ```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/routes -d '{"match":{"session_tokens_gt":3000},"action":{"model":"gpt-open-3b","priority":100}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

maria: rule applied. pushing to edge in ~15s.

leo: added a dashboard panel for KV miss rate + worker GC pause. KV miss rate jumps aligned with p99 spikes. GC traces show a few workers with 800-1200ms pause during compaction.

jordan: ok, we have plausible cause: worker GC + KV cache pressure causing tail stalls. Mitigations in flight. Sam, can you scale up worker pool by +20% in the autoscaler group as temporary buffer?

sam: scaling now: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name streamer-prod --desired-capacity 36` -> request submitted. Should start adding pods in ~60-90s.

maria: p99 trending down to ~500ms after route flip and scale. still above SLO but improving.

ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: create incident ticket and set severity.

jordan: creating incident ticket: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20240315-78 — severity: P2 (customer impact on tail latency). Adding initial notes.

maria: quick customer impact estimate: based on logs, ~2.8% of streaming requests exceed 800ms in the last 10m, concentrated on sessions with >2500 tokens. No error responses observed (200s), so degraded latency only.

jordan: good to note. notify support and scale teams. @leo can you add a list of top customers (by org-id) hitting long sessions? we should inform any high-traffic customers.

leo: running query: top orgs in window: org-842 (1.1k reqs), org-19 (980 reqs), org-504 (110 reqs). org-842 and org-19 have a higher proportion of long sessions.

maria: reached out to account reps for org-842 and org-19: FYI latency degradation, we're mitigating, will follow up in incident postmortem.

sam: autoscaler added 6 instances, pods becoming ready. p99 now ~360ms. Good.

jordan: great. next steps: 1) keep routing rule for 30m, 2) monitor for regressions, 3) run heap/gc profiler on two nodes with highest GC pauses, 4) if p99 returns to normal rollback routing.

maria: starting heap dump on stream-worker-12 and -19: `gcore` in progress (copying to /tmp for analysis).

ops-runbook-bot: Checklist: set incident page, assign scribe, start timeline.

jordan: i'm assigning scribe to @maria. I'll continue oncall and escalate if p99 rises.

maria: scribe accepted. adding timeline notes to INC-20240315-78.

leo: initial root-cause hypothesis: increased KV cache miss rate due to larger-than-expected context growth + GC pressure on a small subset of worker instances causing tail stalls.

sam: after scale and route flip, p99 stabilized below SLO. recommend keeping mitigations for 30-60m while we gather heap dumps and run deeper profiling.

jordan: agreed. closing pager for now but keeping incident open for postmortem. I'll hand off to infra-oncall for follow-up. Thanks everyone. :pray:

ops-runbook-bot: Incident status: acknowledged -> mitigated. Next action: postmortem assigned to eng-ml and eng-runtime.

maria: adding notes: follow-ups: 1) investigate GC tuning and memory footprints 2) KV cache sizing and eviction policy 3) improve early-detect regression thresholds to reduce tail exposure 4) test routing fallback automation.

jordan: handoff to infra-oncall @sam for follow-up and postmortem. If p99 climbs over 800ms again, re-open pager.

sam: got it. I'll coordinate the heap analysis and a temporary GC tuning patch on a small batch.

maria: final p99 snapshot before handoff: 280ms (last 5m). closing active mitigation notes in incident ticket.

IncidentBot: Incident INC-20240315-78 updated: mitigated by routing fallback + autoscale. Postmortem scheduled.

jordan: thanks team. logging final retrospective items in the ticket.

maria: thanks all. :thumbsup:
